title: Predictive slot allocator & KV fragmentation mitigation for mixed-length continuous batching
creator: Alyssa Park
description:
Problem: Our continuous batching scheduler currently struggles with workloads that mix short prompts (few tokens) with much longer responses. Observed issues include: increased P50/P95 latency due to head-of-line blocking, elevated KV cache memory pressure causing allocation spikes and occasional GPU OOMs on 24GB cards, and inefficient packing that reduces effective batch throughput.

Goal: Implement a predictive slot allocator and KV fragmentation mitigation to reduce latency variance and memory overhead while preserving throughput for mixed prompt/response workloads. The work must be safe to roll out and revertable, with telemetry to validate customer-facing metrics.

Scope: scheduler changes (predictive slot allocation, prioritized preemption), KV cache compaction heuristics (tail compaction on sequence end, opportunistic slab coalescing), runtime knobs (slot_hold_ms, max_slots_per_seqlen_bucket, kv_eviction_threshold_percent), and experiment harness + dashboarding for P99/P95 latency, GPU memory utilization, and throughput (tokens/sec).
acceptance_criteria: 1) P95 generation latency decreases by >=15% for mixed-length test workload (mix defined below) without reducing tokens/sec by >5%. 2) GPU memory 95th percentile reduces by >=250MB on 24GB instances under the same workload. 3) No increase in failed/errored requests (error rate stable). 4) Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 flag and reversible with config. 5) End-to-end integration tests + load experiments recorded in perf dashboard.
design_notes:
- Predictive slot allocator: maintain lightweight histogram of recent prompt+response length pairs per model and use exponential smoothing to predict expected response length for an incoming request. Allocate a 'slot' sized to cover predicted active tokens instead of using fixed max. This reduces head-of-line blocking when a short prompt would otherwise wait for long responses. 

- Slot buckets: group sequences into discrete length buckets (e.g., 0-64,65-256,257-1024) with configurable max_slots_per_seqlen_bucket to avoid starvation.

- Preemptive flush / prioritized preemption: if a bucket is backlogged and longer sequences are holding KV slots, allow short sequences to preempt by moving longer sequences into a survival queue that yields GPU memory but keeps KV state on disk or quantized cache. The scheduler will preferentially run short buckets to optimize latency SLOs.

- KV fragmentation mitigation: on sequence completion, mark KV slabs as reclaimable and run opportunistic compaction when reclaimed fraction > kv_compact_threshold. Implement lightweight slab coalescing to reduce fragmentation without a full stop-the-world defragmentation.

- Adaptive eviction policy: use kv_eviction_threshold_percent to trigger LRU-like eviction only for long-lived inactive prefixes; keep recent prefix-cache hot to preserve continuation latency for conversational flows.

- Safety: feature gated; default conservative parameters (slot_hold_ms=150ms, kv_eviction_threshold_percent=75). All knobs exposed via runtime config and traceable by request id.
experiment_results:
Test harness: mixed-length-sim workload: 40% short prompts (<=32 tokens) expecting short responses (~16-64 tokens), 40% medium prompts (<=128) expecting medium responses (~128-256), 20% long prompts (<=512) with long responses (~512-1024).

Baseline (no changes) on a 4xA10 pool: P95 latency=1.42s, P99=3.9s, tokens/sec=185k, GPU mem 95th=10.9GB.

With predictive slot allocator + compaction (conservative knobs): P95=1.18s (-17%), P99=3.1s (-21%), tokens/sec=182k (-1.6%), GPU mem 95th=10.6GB (-300MB). Error rate unchanged. Tail latency improved more for short-bucket percentiles (P50 short-bucket dropped 28%).

Aggressive knobs (slot_hold_ms=80ms, smaller bucket caps): tokens/sec increased to 190k but observed 0.03% transient increase in OOM-like evictions on 24GB cards — reverted during experiment.

Telemetry added: per-request predicted_length, allocated_slot, kv_slab_id, compaction_events, and preemption_events.

Add slot bucketization and allocation API in scheduler core (ENG-15742-2)
KV slab reclamation & opportunistic compaction implementation (ENG-15742-3)
Expose runtime knobs and feature flag (ENG-15742-4)
Integration tests for correctness and reproducibility (ENG-15742-5)
Perf harness run and dashboard config (ENG-15742-6)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind 'predictive_slot' feature flag into runtime-1.22 branch. 2) Internal dogfood: enable for 10% of internal traffic for 72h, collect P95/P99, GPU mem metrics. 3) Expand to 50% for 48h if metrics stable. 4) Gradually ramp to 100% for non-enterprise customers for 1 week, keep enterprise default off; provide opt-in. 5) Monitor for increased preemption events, compaction latency spikes, and OOMs. 6) If regression observed, revert flag and open hotfix.
risks: Predictor misestimation could allocate too-small slots causing more preemption and wasted GPU cycles
Compaction may cause transient CPU/GPU stalls if threshold misconfigured
Preemption semantics for long-running responses could harm throughput for long-sequence-heavy customers
Edge cases with streaming clients holding connections longer than predicted; need client-side TTL coordination
